title: Weather and zero-shot forecasting models: backtest results for GB electricity demand (part 1 of 2)

primary_sources.paraphrase: Zenodo record, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24161799, published 2026-11-12 by Andy Moran (Heaviside Analytics), MIT. Preregistered 960-day day-ahead backtest on GB national demand: three zero-shot models and a weekly-lag regression get the same weather forecasts; weather cuts error for all four and the models' edge over the regression largely disappears.

Results note at the release tag. Half-hourly forecasts of day D issued 09:30 on D-1; error is daily MAE in MW; 16 Mar 2024 to 31 Oct 2026. Tables give each forecaster's error with and without weather, ratios with 90% block-bootstrap intervals, the gap to NESO, splits by release date, season and time of day, pinned revisions and caveats.

Frozen plan at tag weather-plan. Only Q1 (weather improves each of the four forecasters) is confirmatory, four one-sided tests at 0.0125. The comparison with the regression given the same weather (Q3) and the gap to NESO (Q2) are estimates with 90% intervals, no test and no threshold. The live window to 31 Mar 2027 is descriptive.

MIT-licensed repository holding the plans, locks, results and daily prospective forecast manifests; weather_study/ has the plan, lock, results note and scored outputs. The README repeats the weather study's headline numbers and its DOI.

Tag weather-plan points at commit de46eb3 (committer date 2026-11-10 23:50 UTC, a freeze before any forecast with real weather); tag weather-results-backtest points at 4e6c9b3 (2026-11-12 12:08 UTC), after the results note commit.

Commit history of amazon/chronos-2, the central model: weights and config added in commit 95a9710e on 2025-10-30; later commits are README, tag and deployment-guide changes, the latest 29ec3766 on 2026-06-05 (the revision the study pins).
Model record of amazon/chronos-2: licence apache-2.0, head 29ec3766, files config.json and model.safetensors.

relevance.rationale: National electric load at half-hourly resolution, the same kind of series as our hourly zonal load (3). Day-ahead, not week-ahead (2). Archived weather forecasts, timed to what was public at issue, are a known-future input for every forecaster, which is our forecast regime; the study has no oracle-weather arm (3).

checks.notes: pre_registered: the plan, code hashes and inputs were frozen at tag weather-plan (commit de46eb3, committer date 2026-11-10 23:50 UTC), the backtest was scored once on 11 Nov and released on 12 Nov with a DOI. Only Q1 (weather helps each forecaster) is confirmatory; the comparison with the regression (Q3), which is the one our benchmark mirrors, is a pre-specified estimate with no test and no threshold. training_overlap_risk is about our run: the amazon/chronos-2 weights were committed on 2025-10-30 (95a9710e), before the first scored week (2025-11-10), so all scored weeks start after it. independent_replication: two searches found none. Central model: Chronos-2, the only model near the regression once both have weather; Timestral-209M and TimesFM 2.5 are the others. evidence_strength is strong by the spec: pre-registered, 960 days, regression given the same three weather variables; it applies to Q1, while the Q3 ratio is descriptive. In the study's own backtest 593 of 960 days precede Chronos-2's release, and the author names the live window as the clean test. Same-inputs caveat: the regression is fitted on unrescaled reanalysis history while the models' history is rescaled to the forecast source; the note's check puts the effect at about 1 MW. Unverified: the pre-registration timing rests on git committer timestamps and the author's statements (the weather-processing code was private at the freeze; gb-weather-private, the lock file and the hashes were not opened); the Zenodo zip was not opened in this run, the results note was read from the GitHub tag of the same name and assumed identical; numbers were read once through a fetch summary, not from the raw file; the weights commit is inferred from its title, the listing shows no file diffs; the results note calls one regression term wind chill where the plan says temperature times wind.

label: ACCEPT_RUN
label_reason: On-target, pre-registered study with a full public record (plan, results note, scored outputs, DOI) whose headline comparison, Chronos-2 against a lag regression with both given the same weather forecasts, is the one our benchmark already runs. It is day-ahead on GB national demand rather than week-ahead on PJM zones, and the comparison with the regression is a descriptive estimate, so the run tests transfer of the 0.966 ratio, not of a confirmed test result.
implementation_hint: Chronos-2 zero-shot with temperature via models/chronos2.py, weights amazon/chronos-2 (weights commit 95a9710e2596287d08352589f42634fa5abdf0a7, 2025-10-30; the study pins 29ec376, same weights file). Compare with lag_regression_temperature in the forecast regime, per zone: this is the protocol's primary comparison. Claimed ratio 0.966 (0.931 to 1.001) at day-ahead with temperature, wind and solar; ours is week-ahead with temperature only. Secondary: Timestral-209M with temperature (models_ff/run_ff.py, claimed 1.074); TimesFM 2.5 runs univariate in models_ff/run_ff.py, so its 1.453 with covariates needs the direct adapter.

receipt.claimed: Chronos-2 and a weekly-lag regression given the same weather forecasts are about equal day-ahead on GB national demand: error ratio 0.966 (90% interval 0.931 to 1.001), a pre-specified estimate, not a test; the model's edge over the regression largely disappears once the regression has weather.
receipt.horizon_mismatch: The study is day-ahead (half-hourly, issued 09:30 on D-1) on GB national demand over 960 days with temperature, wind and solar forecasts; ours is week-ahead (168 h, hourly) on PJM zones JC and DOM over 48 scored weeks with temperature only. The study's regression is a weekly-lag regression with three weather variables; ours is the temperature-only regression.
